Job Title

QA Program Lead - OmniPay Modernisation

About your role:

We are looking for a QA Program Lead to define and drive the quality strategy across the entire OmnipayNext program.

This is a technical leadership role with program-wide responsibility. You will lead through influence — setting standards, coaching QA engineers and developers across domain teams, and building the frameworks and governance that ensure consistency across a complex, multi-team program. You will be the recognised authority on QA within the program and the go-to person for quality strategy, risk assessment, and testing approach.

The balance is approximately 70% strategy, governance, and stakeholder engagement / 30% hands-on — you set direction and standards, but you also get into the detail: reviewing test automation code, designing cross-domain test scenarios, and validating that approaches are sound, not just documented.

What you’ll do:

  • QA Strategy and Governance: Define and own the program QA strategy, aligned with business, regulatory, and delivery goals. Set testing standards across unit, integration, contract, end-to-end, performance, and security testing. Embed consistent quality gates in CI/CD and deployment workflows with Platform Engineering. Evolve the QA strategy as the program and platform scale.
  • Hands-On Quality Engineering: Own cross-domain tests covering the full transaction lifecycle. Review test automation, schema contracts, and test designs, advising on coverage and approach. Maintain onboarding tests that confirm end-to-end processing before go-live. Support triage and root-cause analysis for cross-domain defects.
  • QA Community Leadership: Lead, mentor, and upskill QA engineers and developers across the program. Run QA community sessions to share knowledge and solve common quality challenges. Identify QA skill gaps and address them through coaching, training, or hiring. Champion shift-left and built-in quality. Drive adoption of AI-assisted test generation, defect prediction, and coverage analysis.
  • Client Onboarding and Migration Readiness: Define go-live criteria for parity, performance, data integrity, and operational readiness. Own onboarding tests that validate configuration and end-to-end processing. Ensure the approach is repeatable and scalable. Curate golden datasets for parity validation across configurations, transactions, and pricing.
  • Non-Functional Quality: Lead performance, resilience, failover, and production-scale load testing. Define back-pressure, retry, and degradation expectations under stress. Validate disaster recovery and failover end-to-end across domains.
  • Stakeholder Engagement and Reporting: Give program leaders clear, actionable visibility of quality status. Turn technical metrics into business indicators for go-live decisions. Escalate cross-domain quality risks before they affect milestones.
  • Test Environments and Data Strategy: Define the AWS EKS test environment strategy with Platform Engineering. Ensure reproducible cross-domain testing with PCI-DSS-compliant test data.

What you’ll need to have:

  • Program-level QA leadership across multiple engineering teams — setting strategy and standards.
  • Deep knowledge of modern QA practices — test automation strategies, shift-left testing, continuous testing in CI/CD, contract testing, and quality engineering principles.
  • Financial services industry experience — payments, acquiring, issuing, or banking.
  • Cloud-native and event-driven architecture experience — microservices, asynchronous event processing (Kafka, message brokers), eventual consistency, schema evolution, and distributed system failure modes.
  • Excellent communication skills — able to engage credibly with engineers, architects, product owners, and senior leadership.
  • Technical credibility — able to read event schemas, understand data models, review test automation code, and assess whether a testing approach is sound.

What would be great to have:

  • Regulated environment experience (PCI-DSS, SOX, or equivalent).
  • Migration or platform replacement validation — proving a new system matches an old one at scale, including defining equivalence criteria and comparison approaches.
  • Experience leveraging AI in QA workflows — using AI-assisted tools for test generation, code review, defect analysis, or standards enforcement.

title: Software Engineer, Senior
description:
About FlightSafety International

FlightSafety International is the world’s premier professional aviation training company and supplier of flight simulators, visual systems and displays to commercial, government and military organizations. The company provides training for pilots, technicians and other aviation professionals from 167 countries and independent territories. FlightSafety operates the world’s largest fleet of advanced full-flight simulators and award-winning maintenance training at Learning Centers and training locations in the United States, Canada, France and the United Kingdom.

Purpose of Position

• Review engineering requirements, simulator specifications, malfunction documentation, test requirements, and aircraft data related to Automatic Flight Control Systems (AFCS), Air Data Systems (ADS), and Fly‑By‑Wire (FBW) systems.
• Develop, integrate, and maintain AFCS, ADS, and FBW simulation software.
• Develop control laws and system models for Flight Director/Autopilot, Yaw Damper, Auto‑Trim, and related auto flight functions.
• Develop Air Data System models including pitot‑static systems, temperature probes, smart probes, and Air Data Computers.
• Develop Fly‑By‑Wire models, logic, and control system behavior.
• Transform engineering flow diagrams into high-order computer language and working simulation models.
• Use model‑based development tools (picture‑to‑code) to create simulation software.
• Integrate Auto Flight and FBW systems with control loading and motion systems.
• Develop test programs, customer test plans, and test guides for AFCS, ADS, and FBW systems.
• Perform standardized checkout procedures for assigned systems.
• Conduct Auto Flight system testing under the direction of a Lead Engineer or Manager.
• Collaborate with other engineering groups to ensure systems meet all test and qualification requirements.
• Participate in on‑site simulator qualification activities.
• Support customer testing, address discrepancies, and ensure systems are ready for customer use.
• Travel, shift work, or customer site support may be required.
• Maintain professional behavior and contribute to a cooperative team environment.
• Protect export‑controlled material and ensure security of technical information.
• Ensure accuracy and completeness of assigned tasks.
• Maintain regular attendance and the ability to work safely and attentively.

Qualifications
• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, preferably Aerospace, Aeronautical, or Electrical (or equivalent experience).
• Experience with FORTRAN, UNIX, C++, and MATLAB preferred.
• Knowledge of Windows, UNIX, Linux, and Concurrent operating systems preferred.
• Experience with scripting languages preferred.
• Ability to read and interpret engineering data, drawings, and specifications.
• Valid driver’s license and ability to obtain a passport.

Work Environment
• Combination of office and simulator lab environments with moderate noise levels.
• Frequent sitting, reaching, talking, and hearing; occasional standing, walking, climbing, or stooping.
• Occasional lifting up to 50 lbs; requires close and color vision.
• Occasional exposure to moving mechanical parts, heights, electrical risk, and vibration.

Tasks and Responsibilities

Develops, supports, and maintains software components, interfaces, features, subsystems, and systems across the development cycle.

Apply skills in requirements identification and analysis; software design and construction; software testing and verification; problem identification and resolution; maintenance and troubleshooting; user support and multi-disciplinary team collaboration.

Apply skills in interpreting schematics, wiring diagrams to create software models of physical systems.

Uses disciplined software development methods, including construction techniques, test methodologies, configuration management, and software tools; uses and contributes to product and process management information systems and documentation.

Mentors and assists other software engineers.

Apply skills in document preparation to create customer test and internal/external user guides.

Apply presentation skills to demonstrate the operation of systems to internal and/or external customers.

Consults with other software and hardware engineers as part of a team. Communicates effectively between departments.

Designs prototypes for new technologies, algorithms, structures, and processes. Conducts research and development.

Supports computer system and hardware requirements, integration, and maintenance.

Develop engineering tools

Remains current on state-of-the-art technologies through technical papers, periodicals, and conferences.

Travel, shift work, and special work hours may be required to accomplish some of the above tasks.

Exhibits and practices professional and courteous behavior while interacting with both internal and external customers.

Interacts within a cooperative environment through beneficial behavior, commitment to common goals, contribution to problem solving, communication of ideas and suggestions, and encouragement to other employees and departments.

Accountable for the control and distribution of documents and/or equipment subject to export control restrictions or other applicable laws and regulations and the security of FSI materials, projects and business information regarding the methods and techniques used in the production and usage of FSI products.

Accountable for the accuracy and completeness of assigned tasks.

Able to adhere to a work schedule including prompt and regular attendance. Willingness to work overtime as necessary.

Adhere to accurate time recording of daily work activity.

Ability to work in a constant state of alertness and in a safe manner.

May be required to apply for and maintain a security clearance.

Minimum Education

Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering or other applicable technical field; and two years related experience; or equivalent combination of education and experience, or Master’s Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering or other applicable technical field preferred.

description:
Calling all innovators – find your future at Fiserv.

Job Title

Operational Business Analyst

About your role:

Reporting to the Programme Director and/or Programme Manager, the role of Operational Readiness Business Analyst is to support client implementations, conversions and migration initiatives by assessing, documenting and coordinating the operational readiness activities required to enable a successful transition into go-live, warranty and business-as-usual.

Working closely with clients, internal Fiserv teams and third-party partners, the Operational Readiness Business Analyst helps ensure that operational processes, support models, controls, procedures, training needs and handover requirements are clearly understood, documented and aligned to the target-state solution and implementation plan.

The Operational Readiness Business Analyst is responsible for supporting readiness activities across the full project lifecycle, from initial impact assessment and readiness planning through implementation support, go-live preparation and transition to BAU. The role acts as a key link between business stakeholders, operations, service and support teams, implementation teams, product, technology and testing teams to help ensure that operational teams are prepared for change and able to support the target operating model effectively.

Within this context, the role requires a good understanding of issuing and card-processing environments, operational processes and the practical impacts of migrating from legacy platforms to modern target solutions.

What you will do:

  • Supporting the definition and coordination of the operational readiness approach in alignment with project and implementation objectives.
  • Assessing current-state and target-state operational processes to identify readiness impacts, gaps, dependencies and required changes.
  • Gathering, analysing and documenting operational readiness requirements across business, service, operations and support teams.
  • Supporting the identification of impacts to operating procedures, service models, controls, escalation paths, support processes and business continuity arrangements.
  • Producing and maintaining readiness documentation, including impact assessments, readiness trackers, process documentation, handover requirements and supporting artefacts.
  • Working closely with implementation, business analysis, product, technology, testing and operations teams to ensure that readiness activities are aligned to the broader programme plan.
  • Supporting the definition and tracking of readiness criteria for key milestones, go-live and transition to BAU.
  • Coordinating with stakeholders to ensure that process changes, support requirements, operational dependencies and handover activities are clearly understood and planned.
  • Supporting training needs assessment and readiness-related communications for impacted teams where required.
  • Identifying, analysing and resolving operational readiness queries raised by stakeholders, internal teams and third-party partners.
  • Supporting go-live preparation by ensuring that operational teams, processes and support arrangements are ready for transition.
  • Acting as a liaison between business, operations, service/support teams and project delivery teams throughout the readiness lifecycle.

Execution & Controls

  • Managing and maintaining operational readiness deliverables in accordance with established Fiserv governance, standards and project methodology.
  • Supporting the planning, prioritisation and tracking of operational readiness activities in line with project milestones, implementation phases and delivery timelines.
  • Ensuring that readiness requirements, dependencies, actions and open points are captured, tracked and progressed to closure.
  • Maintaining operational readiness trackers and supporting the assessment of readiness status across impacted teams and functions.
  • Working with stakeholders to validate readiness criteria, handover requirements and support arrangements prior to go-live.
  • Participating in governance meetings, working sessions and status reviews to provide updates on readiness progress, key issues, risks and unresolved dependencies.
  • Escalating readiness risks, gaps, blockers or delivery concerns to the appropriate stakeholders in a timely and structured manner.
  • Supporting implementation and testing activities where operational readiness input is required, including business process validation and handover readiness.
  • Supporting warranty and BAU transition planning by ensuring that support teams, processes, documentation and responsibilities are clearly defined and agreed.
  • Maintaining clear and consistent communication with clients, internal teams and third parties on operational impacts, readiness actions and transition requirements.

Closeout & Transition

  • Confirming that operational readiness requirements and agreed handover activities have been completed and transitioned appropriately into go-live, warranty and BAU support processes.
  • Supporting the completion and archiving of readiness documentation, including process updates, handover artefacts and supporting records.
  • Assisting with post-implementation reviews to assess readiness outcomes, operational issues and improvement opportunities.
  • Ensuring that outstanding readiness actions, process gaps or follow-up items are tracked through to closure or transitioned appropriately into warranty and BAU support processes.
  • Contributing to Lessons Learned activities where applicable.

Experience you’ll need to have:

  • Proven experience (minimum 5 years) in one or more of the following areas: Operational Readiness, Service Readiness, Business Process Change, Operations, Customer Servicing, Testing, Training, and BAU Handover within the Financial Services industry, in the Cards and Payments sector; experience in card and/or payment processing environments is preferred.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, with professional proficiency in both English and Italian.
  • Good understanding of implementation lifecycles, go-live readiness, handover processes and transition to BAU.
  • Working knowledge of issuing, card-processing and payments operations, with an understanding of how operational requirements translate into service and support.

Experience that would be great to have:

  • Business Analysis, Change Management or Project Delivery certification preferred.
  • Experience supporting migrations from legacy platforms to modern processing platforms.
  • Experience working on multi-country programmes and complex client delivery initiatives.
  • Exposure to operational change, support model design or business readiness activities within issuing or payments environments preferred.

Salary starting at €52,470 - negotiable depending on experience

Job Title

Analyst II, Financial Crimes Compliance - Investigations


About your role:


As an Analyst II, Financial Crimes Compliance - Investigations, you will support investigations related to the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA), anti-money laundering (AML), fraud, and other financial crime risks. You will work closely with compliance, risk, operations, and business partners to review activity, document findings, and support timely case resolution. Your work helps protect Fiserv, its clients, and the financial system through effective risk identification and investigative analysis.


What you'll do:


  • Investigate potentially suspicious activity, onboard high-risk clients, and perform required periodic client reviews
  • Conduct investigations into potentially suspicious activity, financial crime alerts, and referred cases using internal systems, research tools, and documented procedures
  • Identify potential instances of money laundering, terrorist financing, or other suspicious conduct, determining appropriate next steps which may include preparing Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) and/or Currency Transaction Reports (CTRs) as warranted.
  • Document investigative steps, findings, and recommendations in a clear, accurate, and timely manner to support case quality and audit readiness
  • Maintain case queues and complete assigned investigations within established service level agreements, quality standards, and regulatory requirements
  • Analyze data and reporting outputs to identify trends, support investigative decisions, and contribute to continuous improvement of monitoring and review processes
  • Support adherence to Financial Crimes Compliance program requirements, including policies, procedures, and recordkeeping expectations
  • Recognize merchant acquiring red flags and detect irregularities in merchant or consumer behavior.
  • Responsibilities listed are not intended to be all-inclusive and may be modified as necessary.

Experience you'll need to have:


  • 2+ years of experience in financial crimes investigations within a fintech environment, money services business or financial institution.
  • Analytical and investigative experience, including transaction analysis, evidence collection, and pattern identification.
  • Experience using case management systems, transaction monitoring platforms, Microsoft Excel, and research tools to document investigations and analyze activity
  • Experience preparing narratives, summarizing findings, and communicating investigative results to internal stakeholders.
  • Bachelor's Degree required.

Experience that would be great to have:


  • Professional certification such as Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist (CAMS), Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE), Certified Regulatory Compliance Manager (CRCM), or equivalent certification
  • Master's degree, Juris Doctor, or equivalent combination of education, related experience and/or military experience
  • Experience working with Canadian regulations and submitting Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs).
  • Experience with financial crime compliance systems, Power BI, and anti-money laundering transaction monitoring typologies and rules
  • Experience tracking regulatory laws and changes (BSA, OFAC, NACHA, Payment Network rules and regulations) and proactively applying them to business processes and technology initiatives.
  • Experience supporting investigations in a fast‑paced, structured environment, utilizing advanced analytical and research techniques, online research tools, and clear, well‑documented reporting.

How you'll work:

title: Go To Market Lead
description:
About the role:

At Versuni, we believe the biggest opportunities start with bold ideas, but great innovation only
matters when it makes it into consumers’ homes and creates meaningful commercial impact. As
Global Go-to-Market Manager – Breakthrough Innovations, you will be at the heart of making that
happen.

The impact you’ll make:

You will lead the global Go-to-Market agenda for some of our most exciting breakthrough innovations, shaping how, where and when they come to life across markets. From assessing market potential and defining launch strategies, to building compelling commercial stories for retail partners and tracking performance after launch, you will connect strategy with execution and turn innovation into scalable growth. This is a highly visible, entrepreneurial role for a commercially minded leader who enjoys operating across a broad agenda. If you thrive on ambiguity, move naturally between strategic thinking and hands-on execution, and get energy from seeing an idea become a successful business, this could be your next big opportunity. 1. Shape the commercial strategy Be the commercial architect behind our most important new launches. • Identify where to win: assess market potential, consumer opportunity, category dynamics and competitive landscapes to determine where breakthrough innovations can create the greatest impact, defining market prioritisation and launch sequencing. • Build the commercial strategy: translate product innovation and consumer insight into compelling commercial strategies and launch plans that support our growth ambitions. • Connect global ambition with local opportunity: partner closely with Global Marketing, Product and local markets to shape strategies that balance global consistency with local consumer, channel and customer needs. 2. Make breakthrough launches happen Turn strategy into action and create launches that generate excitement with consumers and customers. • Own the global Go-to-Market agenda: lead the end-to-end GTM workstream across multiple breakthrough innovations, establishing clear milestones, launch gates, and ways of working that bring teams together and keep momentum high. • Create stories that win: develop compelling trade narratives, customer presentations and commercial storytelling that clearly articulate why an innovation matters to consumers and why our retail partners should believe in its potential. • Build a scalable launch engine: create and continuously evolve a global Go-to-Market playbook, capturing best practices and making every launch faster, smarter and more effective than the last. 3. Turn launches into scalable growth Launch day is just the beginning. • Stay close to performance: establish clear launch KPIs and monitor sales, distribution, market activation and other commercial indicators to identify opportunities and risks early. • Turn insight into action: work with local markets and cross-functional teams to diagnose performance gaps, implement corrective actions and accelerate growth where opportunities emerge. • Test, learn and scale: capture what works, rapidly share winning practices across markets and create a continuous feedback loop that makes our innovation engine stronger with every launch.

The skills and knowledge you’ll bring:

You are a commercially sharp, highly curious and energetic professional who enjoys connecting the dots between strategy, innovation and execution. You bring: • A Bachelor's or Master’s degree (preferred) in Business Administration, Marketing or a related field; an MBA is a plus. • 7+ years of experience in Go-to-Market strategy, commercial planning, product marketing, category management or a related commercial role within consumer goods; experience in domestic appliances or consumer electronics is highly preferred. • A proven track record of bringing new products to market and scaling them across multiple markets. • Experience working within a local market organisation, ideally combined with exposure to regional or global teams. Strong cross-functional leadership skills and the ability to build alignment without relying solely on formal authority. • Strong commercial acumen and the ability to translate market data, consumer insight and business performance into clear actions. • Excellent strategic thinking combined with a strong bias for action and execution. • Outstanding communication, presentation and storytelling skills, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders and external customers. • Experience creating commercial strategies, business cases, customer presentations and launch plans. Most importantly, you are someone who gets things done. You can zoom out to see the strategic opportunity, zoom in to solve the detail, and bring people with you along the way.

What we’ll give you in return:

• Internationally competitive base salary | benchmarked against global industry and market leaders
• Performance-based Annual Incentive Program | rewarding those who dare and achieve more
• Top of the market pension scheme | with higher-than-average company contributions
• Work from home, commuting and phone allowances | to support your daily commute, home office setup & business connectivity
• Hybrid working model | effectively combining working from the office & home, depending on team dynamics and personal needs
• Working from abroad | for up to 30 days per year, supporting our many international colleagues as well as travel enthusiasts
• Extensive holiday package | additional care and development days, extensive maternity / paternity leave & possibility to purchase days
• Bicycle Plan | possibility to select a company bicycle for daily commute along with accessories & insurance
• Health Insurance Discount | when signing up with our partner insurance
• Gym Membership Discount | to support your focus on health and wellbeing
• Product Discounts | on all Versuni products which are sold under the Philips brand and our other brands
• High growth environment | offering exciting learning and career development perspectives beyond your first role
• Inclusive working culture | we embrace our international community & diversity as competitive advantage

Ready to make an impact?

From developing game-changing air fryers to perfecting the art of coffee making, Versuni’s purpose is turning houses into homes — and we’re calling on your talent to bring it to life. Join our global team of 6,000+ passionate individuals, work with world-class brands, and shape the future of home living. We’re ready for you — are you ready for us?

Job Title

API Security Architect

Calling all innovators – find your future at Fiserv.



We're Fiserv, a global leader in Fintech and payments, and we move money and information in a way that moves the world. We connect financial institutions, corporations, merchants, and consumers to one another millions of times a day – quickly, reliably, and securely. Any time you swipe your credit card, pay through a mobile app, or withdraw money from the bank, we're involved. If you want to make an impact on a global scale, come make a difference at Fiserv.



About your role:

Our API security function is about 18 months in and growing fast, and we're looking for an API Security Architect / SME to step into a role with real impact — not maintaining someone else's playbook, but shaping the strategy and technical direction for a program that's scaling quickly. You'll step into the gap left by the architect who built most of the program, owning API design review, risk profiling, identity, and incident/exploitation analysis, while helping mature our runtime protection strategy (Traceable) and setting the technical direction going forward.




What you'll do:

  • Own end-to-end API security architecture — design review, risk profiling, identity, and incident/exploitation analysis — for a fast-growing, high-scale financial-services API ecosystem.
  • Set the technical direction for the API security program and mature it from where the previous architect left off, rather than simply operating an existing playbook.
  • Guide the strategy behind our runtime protection platform (Traceable), partnering with the engineers who handle day-to-day tuning, false positives, and blocking-mode operations.
  • Design identity and access patterns for APIs (OAuth2/OIDC, JWT, scopes/claims, token handling), closing gaps such as overly broad token authorization.
  • Lead technical investigation of API security incidents and exploitation attempts, translating findings into durable architectural fixes.
  • Partner closely with a strong, hands-on engineering team (including automation/infrastructure-as-code talent) to turn architectural direction into secure API designs.
  • Bring architectural judgment to the table — explain the why, not just the what — across design reviews and cross-team security decisions.
  • Responsibilities listed are not intended to be all-inclusive and may be modified as necessary.



Experience you'll need to have:

  • Significant experience owning API security architecture (or a comparable security architecture discipline), ideally having built or matured a program from the ground up.
  • Hands-on, personal experience with runtime API protection platforms such as Traceable, Salt Security, or NoName — including configuring, tuning, and investigating alerts (not just research-based familiarity).
  • Demonstrated experience designing identity and access patterns for APIs (OAuth2/OIDC, JWT, scopes/claims, token handling).
  • A proven track record investigating and resolving API security incidents or exploitation attempts, with real analytical depth.
  • Strong architectural judgment — the ability to explain the reasoning behind a design decision, not just implement it.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, comfortable working shoulder-to-shoulder with engineering, product, and security teams.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.



Experience that would be great to have:

  • Experience building automation or CI/CD integration for API security (policy-as-code, OpenAPI-based checks, pipelines).
  • Experience in financial services or another highly regulated industry.
  • Relevant certifications (e.g., CISSP, CCSP, or API/security-specific credentials).
  • Experience mentoring engineers or leading cross-functional architecture reviews.
  • A background transitioning from hands-on security engineering into an architecture-level SME role.



How you'll work:

  • This role is on-site Monday through Friday, based at our Alpharetta, GA cybersecurity tech hub where much of the API security team and engineering support is located. Fiserv considers in-person collaboration essential to onboarding, mentorship, and stronger productivity. We're open to other Fiserv cybersecurity locations (e.g., Berkeley Heights, NJ; Columbus, OH; Coral Springs, FL) for exceptional candidates.

  • Experience with cloud-native architectures, event-driven systems, APIs, and real-time transaction processing platforms.
  • Java/Spring Boot experience for building data integration services and APIs.
  • Experience with event-driven ingestion patterns (RabbitMQ, webhooks, retry/idempotency) feeding data pipelines.
  • API and data-validation test automation (RestAssured, Karate, Postman/Newman).
  • Ability to write technical specifications for data integrations and pipelines.
  • Experience applying promotion criteria that include data-quality gates beyond code quality.
  • Hands-on use of AI tools, including AI/ML-enabled data and analytics use cases, with real production examples.
  • Familiarity with running or deploying data workloads on Kubernetes or Red Hat OpenShift.
  • Experience with Snowflake features including data sharing, Snowpark, Streams, Tasks, and performance optimization.

title: Head of Infrastructure - MoneyPass Group
description:
Calling all innovators – find your future at Fiserv.

We’re Fiserv, a global leader in Fintech and payments, and we move money and information in a way that moves the world. We connect financial institutions, corporations, merchants, and consumers to one another millions of times a day – quickly, reliably, and securely. Any time you swipe your credit card, pay through a mobile app, or withdraw money from the bank, we’re involved. If you want to make an impact on a global scale, come make a difference at Fiserv.

Job Title

Head of Infrastructure - MoneyPass Group

Role summary

MPG is a newly standalone payments company running the MoneyPass surcharge-free ATM network, ATM Managed Services and Cash Intelligence software. Our clients are banks, credit unions, fintechs and ATM operators. We are a lean team standing up our own systems while many corporate functions still run on Fiserv transition services, so this leader builds the operating model, not just runs it.

This is a hands-on leadership role, not a purely managerial position. The Head of Infrastructure will personally develop operating processes, configure and administer key platforms where appropriate, troubleshoot complex issues, produce audit evidence, and execute critical implementation work alongside MPG’s managed service providers.

Reports to

Chief Information Officer

Direct reports

None at this time, may include 1-2 as demand increases; leads through the two MSPs and cross-functional partners

Key partners

Head of Security; Finance (vendor spend); Legal and Compliance; business and product leaders for MoneyPass, ATM Managed Services and Cash Intelligence

Location

Remote

Key responsibilities

MSP management: infrastructure (11:11 Systems)

  • Own the 11:11 relationship end to end: contract, statements of work, SLAs, service reviews, escalations and invoices.
  • Define and track operational KPIs (availability, incident response, change success, backup and recovery testing, patch currency) and hold the provider to them.
  • Ensure hosting, network, backup and disaster recovery for production platforms meet MPG's availability and resilience needs.
  • Obtain and review 11:11's own assurance reports (e.g. SOC 1/SOC 2) and map complementary user entity controls MPG must operate.

MSP management: corporate IT

  • Select and onboard the corporate IT MSP (requirements, RFP, due diligence with Security, contract), then own it: end-user support, devices, identity and access, collaboration tools, onboarding and offboarding.
  • Set service levels and a service catalog for employees; run regular service reviews.
  • Own the exit from Fiserv transition services for related IT services, complete by Aug 5, 2027 with no disruption to the business, including supporting data migrations from Fiserv to MPG owned systems.

Partnership with the Head of Security

  • Agree a clear RACI: Security sets policy and risk appetite; Infrastructure implements and evidences controls across both MSPs.
  • Jointly own access management, logging and monitoring, vulnerability management, incident response and change management.
  • Run joint vendor risk reviews of both MSPs, consistent with the vendor-oversight expectations our bank and credit union clients place on us.

SOC 2 Type 1 readiness

  • Lead infrastructure and IT workstreams for a SOC 2 Type 1 audit scoped to Cash Intelligence and Corporate IT under the Security Trust Services Criterion only, with the Head of Security as co-owner. Fiserv remains accountable for SOC 2 for the MoneyPass network and ATM Managed Services.
  • Write or update infrastructure and IT policies and procedures, and ensure controls are designed and in place at the point-in-time audit date.
  • Build evidence collection into MSP operating rhythms so it is repeatable, not a one-time scramble.
  • Support auditor selection, readiness assessment, remediation and the audit itself.

AI-first leadership and adoption

  • Serve as an AI-first leader who identifies and implements practical uses of AI tools and agentic capabilities across infrastructure and corporate IT operations.
  • Use AI-enabled automation to improve service quality, accelerate delivery and maintain efficient operations while keeping internal headcount lean.
  • Champion responsible AI adoption by helping employees and partners build confidence, develop effective use cases and incorporate approved AI tools into everyday work.
  • Ensure AI use complies with MPG’s AI governance framework, policies, security requirements, data-handling standards and applicable legal and regulatory obligations.

Leadership and governance

  • Own the infrastructure and IT budget, including MSP spend and renewals.
  • Report status, risks and SOC 2 progress to executive leadership.
  • Flag and coordinate on anything touching network rules, Regulation E, BSA/AML or bank vendor-oversight obligations with Security, Compliance and Legal.

Qualifications

Required

  • 10+ years in infrastructure and IT operations, including 5+ years leading the function.
  • Proven management of outsourced infrastructure and IT through MSPs: contracts, SLAs, KPIs, escalations and commercial negotiation.
  • Hands-on leadership of at least one SOC 2 (Type 1 or Type 2) or comparable audit, from readiness through report.
  • Working knowledge of hybrid and cloud hosting, networking, identity and access management, backup and DR, and endpoint management.
  • Experience in a regulated industry, ideally payments, banking or fintech.
  • Clear communicator with executives, auditors and vendors.

Desired

  • Experience in a carve-out, spin-off or new company build, including exit from transition services.
  • Experience supporting bank and credit union clients' vendor-oversight reviews as a service provider.
  • Familiarity with ATM networks, card processing or payment switching.
  • Certifications such as CISA, CISSP, ITIL or cloud platform credentials.

This role will perform services for The MoneyPass Group, a company that is jointly owned by Fiserv and Bridgeport Partners. Your employment initially will be with Fiserv , and Fiserv will lease your services to The MoneyPass Group through December 31, 2026. As of January 1, 2027, employment with Fiserv will end and employment will transfer to The MoneyPass Group.

title: Pipeline / Welding Inspector – Subsea Fabrication & Offshore Installation (Ingleside) - Contract
description:
Location: Ingleside, Texas
Site: Subsea 7
Employment Type: Contract - Approximatively 12 weeks but can vary
Certification Required: AWS CWI or CSWIP 3.1 / 3.2

Position Summary

We are seeking an experienced Pipeline / Welding Inspector for a contract assignment in Ingleside, Texas, supporting subsea pipeline fabrication and offshore installation activities.

The ideal candidate will hold a current AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) certification or CSWIP 3.1/3.2 certification and have previous experience with offshore/subsea pipe fabrication.

The assignment will initially support shipyard/fabrication activities and will extend through loadout, transportation, pipelay vessel activities, and offshore installation.

Key Responsibilities

During the shipyard and fabrication phase, responsibilities will include:

  • Review Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs), specifications, and applicable procedures
  • Perform material receiving inspections
  • Verify Material Test Reports (MTRs), material identification, and traceability
  • Witness and review WPS/PQR activities and welder qualification testing
  • Perform fit-up inspections
  • Conduct welding inspections
  • Review NDT documentation and results
  • Perform dimensional inspections
  • Inspect coating and painting activities
  • Inspect riser and spool fabrication
  • Verify anode installation
  • Witness hydrotesting
  • Verify preservation activities
  • Review final inspection and turnover documentation

The inspector will also provide inspection coverage through subsequent project phases, including:

  • Loadout
  • Transportation
  • Pipelay vessel activities
  • Offshore installation
  • Current AWS CWI or CSWIP 3.1/3.2 certification
  • Previous offshore/subsea pipe fabrication experience
  • Strong hands-on experience inspecting pipeline welding and fabrication
  • Experience reviewing WPS/PQRs, welder qualifications, MTRs, NDT documentation, and material traceability
  • Familiarity with coating, dimensional inspection, hydrotesting, preservation, and final documentation
  • Previous exposure to loadout, pipelay vessel, and offshore installation activities is highly desirable
  • Ability to accurately document inspection activities and identify non-conformances
  • Strong understanding of quality control and inspection requirements within a fabrication/shipyard environment.

title: CTI Analyst
description:
Calling all innovators - find your future at Fiserv.

We're Fiserv, a global leader in Fintech and payments, and we move money and information in a way that moves the world. We connect financial institutions, corporations, merchants and consumers to one another millions of times a day - quickly, reliably, and securely. Job Title

CTI Analyst

Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst

Fully on-site | Cybersecurity Operations – Cyber Threat Intelligence



About your role:

Most threat intelligence roles end with a report. This one is built to change what happens next. As a Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) Analyst, you'll be a core member of our Cybersecurity Operations team, reporting to our VP of Cyber Threat Intelligence. Your job is to identify, track, and translate emerging cyber threats into intelligence that protects Fiserv's platforms, clients, data, and infrastructure – for a company that moves money and information millions of times a day.


This is a highly technical CTI seat at the intersection of threat intelligence, incident response, and engineering. You'll work side by side with the SOC, Detection Engineering, Threat Hunting, Attack Surface Management, and Red and Purple Team groups, so your analysis never sits on a shelf – it becomes the detections, hunts, and priorities that come next. If you're naturally curious, love learning new things, and want to explore novel approaches to CTI – including building the tools, models, and platforms that mature a CTI program – this is the seat.



What you’ll do:

  • Operationalize the intelligence cycle by developing and maintaining intelligence requirements, collection requirements, collection plans, and analytic frameworks, then identifying gaps and refining the process to improve outcomes.
  • Produce strategic, operational, and tactical intelligence – threat assessments, campaign analyses, executive briefings, and operational advisories – that inform stakeholders and shape their decisions.
  • Track the threat actors, campaigns, capabilities, and attack patterns that matter most to Fiserv, and use that awareness to set operational priorities.
  • Partner with the SOC and Detection Engineering teams to turn adversary behavior into detection opportunities and prioritized monitoring.
  • Work with the Threat Hunting team to build hunt hypotheses grounded in observed adversary behaviors and trends.
  • Team up with Attack Surface Management to prioritize vulnerabilities using real intelligence on emerging threats, exploitation trends, and attacker adoption patterns.
  • Support Red and Purple Team exercises by profiling relevant threat actors so testing stays realistic and impactful.
  • Dig into adversary infrastructure – domains, IPs, hosting providers, certificates, and operational patterns – to uncover relationships that support investigations and intelligence production.
  • Help build the CTI program of the future by developing and improving intelligence tools, models, processes, and platforms.
  • Responsibilities listed are not intended to be all-inclusive and may be modified as necessary.

Experience you’ll need to have:

  • 5+ years of experience in operational or technical cyber threat intelligence; OR 5+ years of experience in threat hunting, counter-adversary operations, incident response, digital forensics, or related cybersecurity disciplines, with demonstrated knowledge of CTI methodologies and practices.
  • Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field and/or equivalent military or federal experience.
  • Demonstrated ability to apply the intelligence lifecycle, MITRE ATT&CK, cyber kill chain concepts, and adversary TTP analysis to real-world investigations, detections, threat hunts, and intelligence production.
  • Demonstrated ability to conduct threat intelligence analysis, identify attack patterns, develop intelligence assessments, correlate technical indicators, and communicate actionable intelligence to operational and executive stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated ability to evaluate attacker capabilities, assess organizational exposure, and put threats in context for an enterprise environment.
  • Experience using Threat Intelligence Platform (TIP) solutions (e.g., Anomali, OpenCTI) to conduct analysis and support intelligence workflows.
  • Experience working with common CTI providers (e.g., Google Threat Intelligence, Recorded Future, Flashpoint, Silobreaker, CrowdStrike).
  • Experience using security telemetry from network, endpoint, cloud, identity, and/or email security platforms to support analysis, investigations, and threat validation.
  • Strong written communication skills, with the ability to produce clear, concise, relevant intelligence products for a diverse range of stakeholders.
  • Strong verbal briefing skills and comfort presenting threat findings to stakeholders at all levels.



Experience that would be great to have:

  • Relevant certifications such as GCTI, GCIH, GCFA, or similar.
  • Experience in financial services or other regulated environments.
  • Experience conducting malware triage, behavioral analysis, and technical assessments of the malicious tooling adversaries use.
  • Experience performing infrastructure investigations using passive DNS, WHOIS, certificate transparency, internet scanning, NetFlow, and/or related enrichment sources.
  • Experience using Python, PowerShell, KQL, SPL, or similar technologies to automate workflows.
  • Experience running analytical investigations on large datasets, including enrichment, correlation, visualization, and trend analysis across multiple intelligence and security data sources.
  • Experience using LLMs, agentic workflows, or other AI-enabled technologies to support intelligence collection, processing, analysis, and/or production.



How you’ll work:

  • We’re better together! This role is fully on-site at either our Berkeley Heights, NJ office OR our Alpharetta, GA office.
  • This is a full-time, direct-hire position. No contract options or unsolicited agency submissions will be considered.

  • Extensive experience managing enterprise clients at C-suite and VP level, with a consultative, trusted-adviser approach.
  • Strong delivery track record in credit card issuing and large-scale data migration programmes — multiple successful migrations delivered.
  • Practical experience using AI and automation to streamline delivery, governance, and reporting — beyond assistive tooling into embedded and agentic AI.

description:
About the role:

Are you passionate about data, analytics, and understanding what really drives business growth?

As a Data Science Intern – Marketing Mix Modelling, you will join Versuni's Marketing Effectiveness team and work at the intersection of data science, marketing, finance, and business strategy. You'll help uncover the true impact of marketing investments by building analytical models, transforming complex datasets into actionable insights, and supporting decisions that influence millions of euros in marketing spend.

This internship offers a unique opportunity to apply advanced data science techniques to real business challenges. Rather than working on theoretical models, you'll contribute directly to projects that help Versuni determine where, when, and how marketing investments generate the greatest return.

You will work closely with Data Scientists, Data Engineers, Marketing teams, and business stakeholders across the organization, gaining hands-on experience with Marketing Mix Modelling, econometrics, forecasting, and large-scale data analysis. Throughout the internship, you'll develop both your technical expertise and your business understanding, learning how data-driven insights influence strategic decision-making in a global consumer products company.

  • Work hours: 40 hours per week
  • Compensation: 700 Eur
  • Start date: ASAP

  • Extracting data from various sources, bring them together, standardising the data and building ETL pipelines.
  • Building models (time series, linear regressions…) or complex analyses to measure marketing effectiveness.
  • Supporting other data analysts & data scientists with ad-hoc analyses and presentations.
  • Collaborating with data scientists to translate successful prototypes into re-usable solutions, and scale across markets and businesses.

The skills and knowledge you’ll bring:

  • Passion for working with different data sets and bringing them together to solve business problems.
  • Bachelor’s/Master’s degree in a quantitative field such as Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Engineering, Computer Science or Economics, with strong affinity to Marketing.
  • Able to work with data, and with data sources from files and/or databases/systems.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel (Pivot, Lookups, match-index etc.)
  • Experience with Python.
  • Hands-on experience with data wrangling/engineering steps for Extract-Transform-Load activities.
  • Good written & verbal communication skills in English.

Ready to make an impact?

From developing game-changing air fryers to perfecting the art of coffee making, Versuni’s purpose is turning houses into homes — and we’re calling on your talent to bring it to life. description:
Calling all innovators - find your future at Fiserv.

We're Fiserv, a global leader in Fintech and payments, and we move money and information in a way that moves the world. We connect financial institutions, corporations, merchants and consumers to one another millions of times a day - quickly, reliably, and securely. Any time you swipe your credit card, pay through a mobile app, or withdraw money from the bank, we're involved. If you want to make an impact on a global scale, come make a difference at Fiserv.

Job Title

Lead AI Transformation Engineer

About Your Role

As a Lead AI Transformation Engineer, you will play a critical role in advancing AI-driven engineering practices and establishing technical excellence across the Issuer Solutions portfolio. You will work closely with software development and mainframe teams across the organization to drive the adoption of AI-assisted development tools and deliver solutions that align with the business goals and client needs.

What you’ll do:

  • Set and evolve engineering standards (code quality, architecture patterns, CI/CD practices, security posture) across the Issuer Solutions portfolio

  • Conduct solution architecture reviews, code reviews, and design consultations that raise the quality bar for teams building in Java/Spring, .NET, Angular, Python, and related technologies

  • Define reusable patterns, reference implementations, and decision frameworks that teams can adopt independently

  • Bridge the gap between corporate platform teams (AI CoE, Cloud Engineering, Security) and delivery teams by translating enterprise mandates into actionable delivery

  • Champion the adoption and integration of AI-assisted engineering workflows demonstrating measurable impact on quality and throughput

  • Evaluate, pilot, and operationalize AI developer tools across the organization, coaching teams to integrate them into their daily workflows

  • Identify systemic quality issues across the portfolio and propose durable, root-cause solutions by building internal tools and contribute to critical-path code when the situation demands it

  • Deliver technical training and enablement sessions on AI adoption emerging AI-assisted practices while mentoring senior engineers toward deeper architectural thinking, production ownership, AI fluency, and cross-team influence

Experience you’ll need to have:

  • 10+ years of professional software engineering experience, with at least 5 years operating at a staff, principal, or architect level of influence across multiple teams

  • 8+ years of hands-on experience across mainframe and distributed technologies, including Assembler, COBOL, and Java-based enterprise applications, with the ability to bridge legacy and modern architectures

  • 8+ years of experience with CI/CD pipelines, DevOps, and AppOps practices, including production support, monitoring, incident management, and operational excellence

  • 8+ years of experience with cloud-native and containerized environments (OpenShift, AWS/Azure/GCP), with exposure to hybrid mainframe-cloud ecosystems

  • 8+ years of experience with modern databases (SQL, No-SQL) and mainframe data stores where applicable

  • 5+ years of experience in modernizing and integrating mainframe systems with distributed platforms (microservices, APIs, event-driven architectures)

  • 3+ years of experience adopting and championing AI-assisted development tools to improve engineering outcomes at scale

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, or a relevant field, or an equivalent combination of education, work, and/or military experience

Experience that would be great to have:

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills — able to produce clear technical documentation, present to senior leadership, and mentor engineers across platforms and domains

  • Proven track record of driving end-to-end ownership from development through production operations, ensuring reliability, scalability, and performance

  • Solid understanding of application security practices across both mainframe and distributed platforms (encryption, access control, secrets management, vulnerability remediation)

  • Strong experience in AppOps, including performance tuning, resiliency engineering, batch processing, and production stability for mission-critical systems

  • Prior experience in the financial services industry

How you’ll work:

  • Fiserv emphasizes in-person collaboration to help you grow your career while shaping the future of fintech, this role is on-site Monday through Friday

  • This role requires use of a computer and audio equipment

Travel:

  • Approximately 10% travel off-site or to other office locations is expected

Sponsorship:

  • In order to be considered, you must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. without need for visa sponsorship now or in the future

Job Title

Design System Program Manager

About your role:

As a Design System Program Manager for the UniFi Enterprise Design System, you will help operationalize a unified design system that serves as the foundation for design, engineering, accessibility, content, research, and AI-enabled delivery across the enterprise. You will create the structure, governance, communication, and operating rhythm needed to align teams, coordinate work across multiple disciplines, and drive successful adoption of UniFi at scale. You will partner closely with Design, Product, Engineering, Research, Accessibility, Content Design, and business stakeholders to turn strategy into measurable outcomes


What you'll do:

  • Lead program planning, governance, and execution activities that support the successful growth and adoption of the UniFi Enterprise Design System.
  • Coordinate roadmaps, dependencies, release planning, and delivery activities across Design, Engineering, Product, Research, Accessibility, Content Design, and AI teams.
  • Facilitate governance processes, committee reviews, decision forums, stakeholder communications, and executive reporting to ensure transparency and alignment.
  • Drive adoption, onboarding, migration planning, change management, community engagement, and enablement programs that help teams successfully adopt UniFi.
  • Develop dashboards, scorecards, metrics, and reporting frameworks that connect adoption, reuse, governance participation, delivery acceleration, and business value realization.

Experience you'll need to have:

  • 10+ years of experience in Program Management, Design Operations, Product Operations, Strategy & Operations, or a related field.
  • 10+ years of experience managing complex cross-functional initiatives involving multiple stakeholders, teams, and business functions.
  • 7+ years of experience applying systems thinking to integrate products, processes, and operating models across complex enterprise ecosystems, aligning interdependent teams and platforms toward shared outcomes.
  • Strong understanding of modern digital product development, Agile planning practices, and enterprise delivery models.
  • Exceptional communication, facilitation, stakeholder management, and executive reporting skills.
  • Proven ability to influence outcomes, manage dependencies, resolve risks, and drive alignment without direct authority.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience in design, human-computer interaction, or a related field.

Experience that would be great to have:

  • Experience supporting enterprise Design Systems, UX Platforms, Product Platforms, or Centers of Excellence.
  • Familiarity with Figma, Storybook, design tokens, component governance, and design system adoption programs.
  • Experience leading organizational change management, platform migrations, or enterprise transformation initiatives.
  • Experience working with Jira, Azure DevOps, Airtable, Smartsheet, or similar planning and delivery tools.
  • Experience supporting AI-enabled product delivery, design-to-code workflows, or digital transformation efforts within regulated industries.
